title: 1.1.3c Unit 1.1 Quiz
description: Short-answer check on types, variables, vocabulary, and style — closes Unit 1.1. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Answer all four parts. Label each part (A, B, C, D) in your response.

Part A — Data types. For each expression, write what `typeof` returns:
1. typeof "42"
2. typeof 42
3. typeof true
4. typeof undefined
5. typeof null

Part B — Fix the declarations. Each line below is broken. Rewrite it correctly AND say in a few words what was wrong:
1. let 2cool = true;
2. const userName;
3. let user-name = "Al";

Part C — Vocabulary. Define each term in your own words (one sentence each):
1. variable
2. constant
3. data type
4. comment

Part D — Style violations. Each snippet runs but breaks the class style guide. Name the violation in each:
1. let x=5
2. let UserName = "Al";
3. let p = 29.99;

rubric.title: Part A: typeof results correct
rubric.description: Correct answers: 1) "string", 2) "number", 3) "boolean", 4) "undefined", 5) "object" (the famous null-is-object quirk). Full credit if at least 4 of 5 are correct, including a reasonable attempt on null. Deny if Part A is missing or most answers are wrong.

rubric.title: Part B: declarations fixed with reasons
rubric.description: Expected fixes: 1) a name cannot start with a digit (rename, e.g. twoCool / isCool); 2) a const must be initialized when declared (const userName = "..."); 3) names cannot contain a hyphen — use camelCase (userName). Full credit if at least 2 of 3 are corrected AND the student says what was wrong. Partial reasoning is fine for beginners.

rubric.title: Part C: four terms defined
rubric.description: variable = a named container for a value; constant = a variable that cannot be reassigned (const); data type = the kind of value (number, string, boolean, etc.); comment = text the computer ignores, a note for humans. Full credit if all four are defined accurately in the student's own words. Three solid definitions earns partial.

rubric.title: Part D: style violations named
rubric.description: Expected: 1) no spaces around `=` (and missing semicolon) — should be let x = 5; 2) variable name should be camelCase (userName), not PascalCase UserName; 3) `p` is not a descriptive name — use something like unitPrice. Full credit if at least 2 of 3 violations are correctly identified.
